rules.title: How to play
rules.intro: You have five numbered tiles. Everyone can see them except you. Whoever works out their own numbers first wins.
rules.setup1: Each player gets one tile of each colour, at random.
rules.setup2: Your tiles are arranged from lowest to highest. Everyone can see that order, but you cannot see the numbers.
rules.setup3: Five more tiles are turned face up, one of each colour: that is the visible pool. The rest form the reserve, face down.
rules.turnIntro: On your turn you do two things, always in this order:
rules.turn1: Pick a colour and a random tile of that colour comes out of the reserve. It goes into the visible pool and everyone sees its number.
rules.turn2: Pick a tile from the visible pool and ask one of these two questions about your own tiles:
rules.classify: Which two of my tiles does this one fit between? The answer tells you how many of your tiles are lower: “below all of them”, “between tile 2 and tile 3”, “above all of them”…
rules.compare: Does it have the same bars as this tile of mine? The answer is yes or no.
rules.bars1: At the bottom of every tile there are three bars, filled in one, two or three. It is one more clue: two tiles with the same number of filled bars are a match.
rules.bars2: The answer to Compare hangs under the tile of yours you asked about, with the reserve tile you used:
rules.barsSame: Upright: it has the same bars as yours.
rules.barsDifferent: Turned on its side: it has a different number of bars than yours.
rules.turn3: The tile you use is spent and stays in view. Clues and their answers are public: you can also learn from what others ask.
rules.declare1: When you think you know your five numbers, declare. You can do it at any moment, even outside your turn.
rules.declare2: You only get one chance in the whole game. Get all five right and you win on the spot. Get one wrong and you are out: you will see your numbers and can keep watching.
rules.end1: The first player to declare correctly wins, or the last one still in the game.
rules.end2: If the reserve runs out and one more round passes without a winner, it is a draw.
rules.time1: Each turn lasts 60 seconds. If you run out, the server plays for you: it reveals a random colour and places that tile.
rules.time2: Three timed-out turns in a row count as leaving the game.
rules.modePractice: Practice: against 1 to 3 bots. To learn without pressure. It does not count for ELO.
rules.modeRoom: Private room: create a room, share the code and play with whoever you like. It does not count for ELO.
rules.modeRanked: Ranked: against an opponent at your level. It counts for ELO and the leaderboard. You need an account.
rules.tip: Open the deduction board: cross out what you rule out and note candidates for each of your tiles. Anything already visible on other tiles is crossed out for you.

tutorial.title: Tutorial
tutorial.retry: That's not it. Go over the clues and try again: in the tutorial you can retry.

board.title: Your tiles
board.body: These five are yours: everyone can see their numbers except you. Quipu's, on the other hand, you can see. Whoever works out their own numbers first wins.

order.title: Always in order
order.body: You have one tile of each colour, laid out from lowest to highest. You don't know the numbers, but you do know the order: the leftmost is the smallest. This will be key.

reveal.title: Reveal
reveal.body: Each turn has two parts. First you reveal: pick a colour and a tile comes out of the reserve for everyone to see. Tap the amber tile.

classify.title: Classify
classify.body: Now ask for a clue about your tiles. Tap the 31 that just came out, choose Classify and ask: it tells you which of your tiles it fits between.

classified.title: Below all of them
classified.body: The 31 fits below all of them: your five numbers are greater than 31. The clue stays under your row for everyone to see, and the 31 can't be used again.

botTurn.title: Quipu's turn
botTurn.body: Now Quipu plays. Its clues are public too, and every tile that comes into view is a number that can't be yours.

reveal2.title: Your turn again
reveal2.body: First, reveal. This time tap the blue tile.

compare.title: Compare
compare.body: Tap the 60 and choose Compare. Then tap your blue tile, the fifth one, and ask: you'll learn whether both have the same filled bars.

compared.title: Same bars
compared.body: The 60 sits upright under your blue tile: that means yes, both have the same filled bars (three). Had it been turned on its side, the answer would have been no. You can already work out a lot.

deduce.title: Deduce
deduce.body: Think about your blue tile. It's greater than 31 and has three filled bars. Of the blue tiles with three bars, only the 45 and the 60 are greater than 31, and the 60 is in plain sight: it has to be the 45. On the board, tap your blue tile and note down 45.

deduced.title: Well spotted!
deduced.body: On the board, whatever is already in view is crossed out for you, and you cross out what you rule out. With 45 settled, the rest follows in a chain.

declare.title: Declare
declare.body: The amber one is between 31 and 45: 36 or 41. If it were 41, the pink would have to be 43 and the red 44, but 44 is in view. So it's 36, and the same way you get 38, 39 and 42. Type them in and declare.

declareNote.title: Only one chance
declareNote.body: In a real game you can only declare once: get all five right and you win; miss one and you're out. Open Declare when you've got it.

done.title: You know how to play!
done.recap1: Each turn: reveal a colour and ask for a clue with a tile in view.
done.recap2: Clues are public: learn from everyone else's too.
done.recap3: Declare when you're sure: you only get one chance.

prompt.title: First time?
prompt.body: Learn to play in three minutes with a guided game.
